body: Symbol of Sri Lankan HeritageIn the evening on 22nd December 2025, my wife and I visited the Katharagama Kiri Vehra, one of the most revered ancient stupas in Sri Lanka, believed to have been built in the 3rd century BC. Kiri Vehera is a powerful symbol of Sri Lankan Heritage.The Stupa is 29metres tall with a circumference of 85 metres constructed as a bubble shaped dome built from brick and coated with white lime plaster. The name "Kiri Vehera" [Milk Stupa] is attributed to its milky whiteness.The sun falling on the stupa, on that evening, made the white dome glow in a golden colour. We walked around the stupa in a clockwise direction, as is the tradition, and joined the other devotees in worship, offering flowers, incense, lighting oil lamps and meditation. We spent about an hour at the stupa enjoying its serene and spiritual atmosphere.
title: Symbol of Sri Lankan Heritage

body: A group of six of us visited Katharagama Stupa and Devalaya in the evening on 11th February 2019. Our driver dropped us off at the northern entrance to Kirivehera. We were to be picked up at the other end (close to Cargills Food City) after completing our trip to both Kirivehera Stupa and Devalaya. We purchased some flowers from vendors, left our footwear with a caretaker near the entrance and climbed the steps leading up to Kirivehera Stupa. The stupa looks like a bubble and was majestically milky white in the evening against the blue sky. Kiri-vehera literally means milk-temple. We walked all around the ancient stupa that has a circumference of 86 metres and a height of 29 metres. We paid homage by placing our flowers on a flower table. Some of us sat on the ground and joined other praying devotees. There are large encased oil lamps where devotees pour oil for them to burn continuously. No joysticks, candles or other oil lamps are permitted within the surrounded area. The specifically built locations for lighting oil lamps and joysticks are at the lower level away from the main Stupa presumably to avoid discolouration and damage. Walking around the Stupa made me feel calm, tranquil and peaceful. It was not so crowded as it was a normal weekday. The stupa and environs throng with devotees during weekends and holidays and more so on full moon days.Kirivehera is one of the most sacred Buddhist sites in Sri Lanka. It is said to have been constructed in 3rd century BCE, but renovated on several occasions. The legend has it that the Stupa had been built in the location where Buddha rested at Kataragama during his third visit to Sri Lanka. The Kirivehera and Katharagama Devalaya are inseparable to devotees as all those who visit one would visit the other. Just like others, we too were on our way, along the 550 metre gravel road, to the Devalaya after exiting the Kirivehera. Quite close to the exit are a shrine dedicated to “Dedimunda” as well as statues of “Maithree bodisathwa” and “Mahamaya”. Along the way we met many old parents, some on wheel chairs, assisted by their children and grandchildren coming over to pay homage to this hallowed Stupa.Entry to both Kirivehera and Devalaya are free. However, many devotees make a voluntary contribution towards development and upkeep of Kirivehera at the offices located about 50 metres down the road from Kirivehera to the Devalaya.There are notices requesting visitors and pilgrims to remove their footwear before entering the hallowed premises. Visitors are also requested to dress in appropriate attire becoming to a holy place.
title: Milky White Dome - Sacred Buddhist Place of Worship

body: Kirivehera ( which means white pagoda in Sinhalese) is such a spiritual and sacred place that one must visit, if traveling to Kataragama in Sri Lanka. This amazing pagoda and surrounding will surely relax your mind and body and bring you to a place of peace and spirituality irrespective of what ever religion you practice. An ideal time would be early morning and/ or late evening to visit this pagoda. Don’t forget to purchase some lotus flowers from the many flowers vendors and make an offering !Please ensure to wear appropriate clothing (length below knee and having sleeves ) as this is a religious place of worship where many pilgrims come on a daily basis.
